summary: Request timeouts for long-context prompts and large max_tokens (customer-facing)
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports repeated request timeouts (HTTP 504 / streaming disconnects) when sending long-context prompts combined with large max_tokens values. Problem observed across multiple jobs and model variants.

Impact:
- Affects Acme HealthTech production inference for clinical summarization pipelines.
- Several jobs failing intermittently; downstream workflows retry and increase latency/cost.
- Customer experiencing ~20% failure rate for requests with prompt length > ~40k tokens or max_tokens >= 12k.

Environment:
- Redwood hosted prod (us-east)
- Customer dedicated capacity (dedicated GPU pool)
- Models: redwood-v1-large, open-llama-13b

Steps to reproduce:
1) Send a non-streaming generate request with a 40k+ token prompt + max_tokens=12000 to redwood-v1-large in us-east.
2) Observe that request either stalls in the scheduler queue for ~30-50s and then returns 504, or the streaming connection drops after ~60s.
3) Increasing concurrency or switching to a smaller max_tokens tends to reduce failures.

Expected behavior:
- Long but supported context + large max_tokens should either stream partial outputs or complete within SLO or be gracefully queued with backpressure rather than 504.

Actual behavior:
- Requests time out (504) or stream disconnects occur consistently for very long contexts / large max_tokens. Logs show long scheduling/queueing delays followed by API gateway timeout.

Logs / trace snippets (redacted):
- request_id=7a1f3b2d trace_id=tx-9812 status=queued duration=32000ms scheduler_queue_len=42
- serving-runtime: alloc_kv_cache=9.2GB total_mem=62GB decode_start_delay=18000ms
- api-gateway: upstream_read_timeout after 60000ms for request_id=7a1f3b2d

Attachments:
- Customer-provided request examples and timestamps (attached to ticket).

investigation:
Summary of findings:
- Reproduction: Engine team reproduced increased scheduler queueing and decode stalls when prompt_size > ~40k tokens and max_tokens >= 12k under realistic concurrency.
- Root causes hypothesized: (1) KV cache memory pressure leading to eviction and re-population overhead during long decodes; (2) batching policy coalesces long-running requests into large batches which increases decode latency; (3) API gateway upstream_read_timeout (60s) triggers on requests that spend time queued + decode startup.
- Evidence: per-worker metrics showed decode_start_delay spikes (15-25s) and allocator fragmentation. Router logs show queue lengths correlated to customer job peaks.

Next steps in investigation:
- Add tracing to measure time spent in queue vs decode vs network for long-context requests.
- Run a controlled load test to confirm whether changing batching thresholds or enabling early streaming heartbeats eliminates timeouts.
- Evaluate KV cache sizing/eviction policy for dedicated pools and consider higher per-tenant cache reservation.

Action items assigned:
- Diego Morales: instrument allocator and add additional logs (in progress).
- Lena Hoffman: schedule controlled load test in staging and prepare rollback plan for routing changes (in progress).
- Ethan Chen: coordinate customer communication and follow-up documentation (in progress).
resolution:
Temporary mitigations applied on 2026-03-03: increased per-customer concurrency and rerouted traffic to a less-loaded GPU pool; customer failure rate reduced to ~3%.

Permanent mitigations planned / in progress:
- Runtime change to emit early streaming heartbeats so API gateway keeps connection alive during long decodes (PR opened).
- Prioritized scheduling for long-running decode tasks to avoid head-of-line blocking by many short requests.
- Tuning batching thresholds to avoid creating overly large batches that amplify decode time for long-context jobs.
- Evaluate/implement per-tenant KV cache reservations for dedicated pools.

Follow-ups:
- Postmortem and runbook updates (owner: Ethan Chen) to document recommended customer patterns for very long-context jobs (chunking, streaming, model selection) and guidance for Dedicated customers.
- Internal ticket INT-4412 created to track scheduler/runtime changes (linked).

Customer communication plan:
- Shared temporary mitigation and recommended workarounds on 2026-03-03.
- Will provide timeline for permanent fix after load-test results (ETA for timeline by 2026-03-10).
